Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this. We are updating our data retention policy and need to confirm how Redwood handles backup retention overrides and deletion propagation across regions. A few specific asks from our security and audit teams:

- If a primary snapshot is deleted due to retention expiry or a customer-initiated erasure, how and when does that deletion reach DR/offsite replicas?
- Is there a tombstone/marker model you use (i.e., tombstone -> background compaction -> expunge)? Typical auditor ask is: can we demonstrate the chain of custody for an object from delete request to final expunge.
- What are the SLAs/expected windows per region for a deletion to be reflected in restore points? Do you differentiate by storage class (hot vs. cold)?
- We may need a small artifact bundle for our SOC2 auditor showing retention policy, the deletion propagation sequence, and a sample event timeline.

I've attached a short questionnaire. Please let us know the best contact for technical evidence and an expected ETA for the artifact bundle.

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and we can follow with the artifact bundle tomorrow:

- Deletion model: Redwood marks objects with a tombstone and propagates that marker through the replication pipeline. Actual expunge is asynchronous and depends on garbage collection (GC) windows and legal-hold flags.
- Timeline: for same-region replicas we expect tombstone propagation within minutes; cross-region/DR replicas typically observe the marker within 1–6 hours depending on queue/backlog and network retransmission. Final expunge (physical removal) is typically aligned with the next GC window (usually 24–72 hours) unless immediate expunge is triggered by a legal process.
- Storage classes: retention/expiration triggers are applied at snapshot level; archival/cold restores may retain immutable copies for configured retention, and those follow the same tombstone propagation but expunge cadence can be slower for deep archive tiers.

Laura and Ben are copied — Laura can provide the diagram of the deletion handshake and a sample timeline; Ben will pull the playbook and an example audit export. Expect a short artifact bundle by EOD tomorrow.

Would you prefer the artifact bundle as a ZIP with signed manifests, or a shared Drive link plus a short narrative?

Best,
Rishi

Hi Maria — adding the technical sequence here so auditors have something to map to:

1) User/request triggers deletion request (API call / legal erasure job).
2) Control plane writes a tombstone entry to the metadata store (versioned). Tombstone includes: object id, originating region, retention override metadata, request id, and legal hold flag.
3) Tombstone is placed on the replication pub/sub queue. Consumers in each replica region pick up the tombstone and mark local copies as deleted (soft-delete).
4) For active shards we maintain a short TTL-compatible index so snapshots/restore points stop referencing the object immediately after tombstone is accepted. That prevents new restores from including the deleted object.
5) Background GC compaction sweeps remove soft-deleted blobs according to retention and safety windows; compaction writes expunge events to the audit log. Expunge events are the proof that object data was physically removed.

Notes:
- Safety windows are configurable per account; default cross-region safety window is 48 hours.
- If an account has a legal hold, tombstones are written but expunge is deferred; expunge events will be absent until legal hold is cleared.
- We publish expunge events to the audit log with event ids you can reference during an attestation.

I'll attach a simple sequence diagram (PNG) and a sample audit-event JSON (redacted). We can redact internal ids for the auditor package.

Laura Bennett
